newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ministry may sell "Big Three" bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ministry may sell "Big Three" bank shares.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Friday it may sell some holdings in the island's three biggest banks -- Chang Hwa, First Commercial and Hua Nan -- to alleviate the government's budget deficit.
"We are discussing whether we should sell the shares before their prices hit the targets that we previously had set as the selling threshold," a ministry official said by telephone.

He said the ministry previously had planned to sell T$1.837 billion worth of First Commercial shares at the price of T$176 per share, T$233 million worth of Huan Nan at T$188 and T$1.632 billion worth of Chang Hwa at T$184.
Chang Hwa, First Commercial and Hua Nan closed at T$155, T$166 and T$127.50 respectively in Thursday's market.
"Now we are considering the possibility of selling the shares before they hit the target prices due to the immediate budget deficit," the official said.
The government, dogged by a shortfall in tax revenue amid a slow economy in the first three quarters, has forecast a 1996 deficit of T$87.6 billion.
The official declined to say what the new selling price targets for the three banks might be.
